title: PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE SERVICE CONTRACT FOR STANDBY DIESEL GENERATORS
description: Attachment A Performance Work Statement (PWS) STATEMENT OF WORK D5090 - LOW VOLTAGE STANDBY DIESEL GENERATOR PLANNED MAINTENANCE AND INSPECTION SERVICES Table of Contents GENERAL INFORMATION PROJECT REQUIREMENTS DESCRIPTION OF EQUIPMENT GENERAL REQUIREMENTS SCOPE OF WORK - GENERATOR PLANNED MAINTENANCE AND INSPECTION OPTION 1 - LOAD BANK PLANNED MAINTENANCE AND INSPECTION OPTION 2 - AUTOMATIC TRANSFER SWITCH PLANNED MAINTENANCE AND INSPECTION OPTION 3 - DAY TANK PLANNED MAINTENANCE AND INSPECTION DELIVERABLES APPLICABLE PUBLICATIONS 1. GENERAL INFORMATION The United States Embassy in Conakry requires professional services and contractor cost proposals to perform Planned Maintenance and Inspection services of the facility's Low Voltage Diesel Standby Generator systems. 1.1 CONTRACT SCOPE AND LIMITATIONS A. Standby Service - Standard Application This contract is designed for diesel standby generators in emergency/standby service. The standard maintenance schedule assumes: Infrequent operation (emergency use and regular testing only) Typical annual operating hours are less than 200 hours Calendar-based maintenance intervals (two visits per year) B. Prime Power and High-Utilization Applications While the maintenance tasks in this SOW are applicable to prime power and continuous duty operations, the service visit frequency and scheduling must be modified for these applications. Posts operating generators in the following modes must notify the Contracting Officer prior to solicitation to adjust service intervals and pricing: Prime power or continuous duty operations Peak shaving or co-generation systems High-frequency operation (>200 hours annually) Extended run-time operations For these applications: Maintenance intervals shall follow manufacturer's hour-based schedules rather than calendar-based Service visit frequency shall be increased (typically quarterly or more frequently) Additional monitoring and testing requirements may apply Pricing structure must account for increased service frequency and consumables usage C. Service Visit Frequency - Standby Service For standard standby service, this contract provides TWO (2) scheduled maintenance visits per year: One (1) Semi-Annual service (every 6 months �30 days) One (1) Annual service (every 12 months �30 days) Additional visits, major repairs, or component replacements require separate purchase orders. D. Hour-Based Maintenance Triggers Certain manufacturer-required maintenance is triggered by operating hours regardless of calendar intervals (e.g., valve lash adjustment, oil changes, major services). The Contractor shall: Record operating hours at each service visit Notify the COR when generators approach hour-based maintenance intervals Follow the more frequent calendar-based or hour-based schedules per manufacturer�s recommendations Perform hour-based maintenance at the next scheduled visit if within acceptable range, or coordinate additional service if immediate attention is required 2. PROJECT REQUIREMENTS The Contractor shall perform planned maintenance and inspections as described in this Statement of Work (SOW). The intent of this SOW is to ensure the entire standby generator systems for this facility are maintained according to manufacturer's recommendations and to ensure the readiness and proper operation of the system. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform professional Planned Maintenance and Inspection services for the facility's Low Voltage Diesel Standby Generator systems as defined in this Statement of Work. Objectives: Ensure all standby generator systems are maintained according to Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) recommendations Ensure readiness and proper operation of generator systems for emergency power supply Maintain compliance with NFPA standards for generator installation and grounding Prevent equipment failure through regular planned maintenance Extend equipment service life through proper maintenance practices 3. DESCRIPTION OF EQUIPMENT The equipment to be maintained includes: Diesel Standby Generators (See equipment list in attachment) OPTION 1: Load Banks OPTION 2: Automatic Transfer Switches OPTION 3: Day Tanks 4. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS The Contractor shall provide the labor and materials required to carry out regularly planned maintenance and inspections as outlined in this SOW. NOTE: The intent is for the Contractor to supply labor, fluids, filters and items that can be anticipated on a schedule such as coolants and batteries. Repairs or replacement parts should be separately priced. There should be a plan and oversight to avoid unnecessary maintenance/charges or not replacing items such as hoses when necessary. A. Materials and Supplies The Contractor shall inventory, supply and replace maintenance service items (e.g., filters and fluids). Only fluids and parts which meet or exceed manufacturer's specifications shall be used. All fluids shall be delivered in original sealed containers. Contractor shall supply the parts required in performance of maintenance included in this SOW (e.g., rocker cover gaskets when performing valve lash, thermostats when performing coolant change). B. Expendable and Common Parts The Contractor shall maintain a supply of expendable and common parts so that these are readily available for normal maintenance to include: hoses, belts, oil, chemicals, coolant, filters, generator starting batteries, grease, sealant, thermostats, fuses; in addition to the appropriate tools, testing equipment, safety shoes and apparel for technicians, personal protective equipment (hands, hearing, eye protection), MSDS, cleaning material and oil spill containment kits. C. Exclusions This contract does NOT include repair of equipment and replacement of hardware (e.g., bearings, pistons, piston rings, crankshaft, gears, injectors) except as indicated in the maintenance schedules and equipment list. Hardware replacements will be separately priced out by the Contractor for the Government's approval and acceptance. The Government has the option to accept or reject the Contractor's quote for parts and reserves the right to obtain similar spare parts from other competitive sources. If required by the Government, the Contractor shall utilize Government-purchased spare parts, if awarded the work. Such repairs/replacements will be accomplished by a separate purchase order. However, this exclusion does not apply if the repair is to correct damage caused by Contractor negligence. Replacement/repair of any electronic or electrical parts must be approved by the COR prior to installation of the part. If the Contractor proceeds to replace any electronic or electrical parts without COR approval, the Contractor shall de-install the parts at no cost to the Government. D. Checklist Approval The Contractor shall submit to the COR a schedule and description of planned maintenance tasks which the Contractor plans to provide. The Contractor shall prepare this schedule and task description in a checklist format for the COR's approval prior to contract work commencement. E. Manufacturer's Recommended Maintenance It is the responsibility of the Contractor to perform all manufacturers recommended planned maintenance as well as planned maintenance recommended by the manufacturer technical manuals for standby operations of the respective equipment. This does not include major maintenance, planned overhauls, or injector replacements. F. Personnel, Tools, Consumable Materials and Supplies The Contractor shall provide trained technicians with the appropriate tools and testing equipment for scheduled maintenance, safety inspection, and safety testing as required by this Contract. The Contractor shall provide all of the necessary materials and supplies to maintain, service, inspect and test all the systems to be maintained. G. Safety & Special Instru

title: JANITORIAL SERVICES FOR ARMED FORCES RECRUITING FACILITIES LOCATIONS IN PUERTO RICO
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Jacksonville District, is issuing this Request for Proposals (RFP) for a non-personal services contract to provide janitorial cleaning services at Armed Forces Recruiting Facilities located throughout Puerto Rico. The Contractor shall provide all management, supervision, inspections, personnel, equipment, tools, supplies, materials, transportation, and other items and services necessary to perform the requirements of the contract, except for those items specifically identified as Government-furnished. Contractor personnel shall remain under the supervision and control of the Contractor. The Government will not exercise supervision or control over Contractor personnel performing services under this contract. Janitorial services shall be performed in designated areas identified in the Performance Work Statement (PWS), including, but not limited to, hallways, restrooms, offices, work areas, entranceways, lobbies, common areas, testing areas, and storage areas. The Contractor shall also perform pest control and HVAC maintenance services in accordance with the applicable requirements, frequencies, performance standards, and quality requirements established in the PWS. The Contractor shall perform all services in accordance with the terms and conditions of the solicitation, PWS, applicable attachments, and all applicable Federal, Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and local laws and regulations. The anticipated contract will be Firm-Fixed-Price with one (1) base year period and four, one (1) year option periods. The anticipated period of performance is October 1, 2026, through September 30, 2027. This acquisition is being solicited as a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned (SDVOSB) set-aside. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 561720, with a small business size standard of $22M. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the complete solicitation, PWS, pricing schedule, attachments, and any amendments issued for this requirement. Proposals shall be submitted in accordance with the solicitation instructions and no later than the date and time specified in the solicitation.

title: Renewable Energy Credits
description: (This is not a Request for Quotations; this is for market research purposes Sources Sought only) The Architect of the Capitol (AOC) requires the establishment of a contract to support the Capitol Power Plant�s acquisition of Renewable Energy Certificates. The resulting contract shall consist of one (1) base year and four (4) one-year option periods. This requirement shall be solicited and awarded as a firm-fixed-price contract. 1.0 General. Renewable Energy Credits 1.1 Short Description. The AOC is requesting proposals for the supply of Renewable Energy Credits (RECs) for various electrical accounts. The contract will have a base year and four (4) option years and will be priced per the total megawatt hours requested by AOC. Contractor shall supply the full REC requirement by the due date for deliveries for the base year and if exercised the option years. 1.2 Background. The Architect of the Capitol (AOC) manages approximately 18.4 million square feet of building space in over 50 buildings and 570 acres of land. The AOC has been directed by the Energy Independence and Security Act (EISA) of 2007 to continue to develop, update and implement cost effective energy comprehensive energy management and water conservation plans for all facilities administered by Congress to meet energy performance requirements for Federal buildings. In prior fiscal years, the AOC purchased RECs as a percentage of the energy procurement through the General Services Administration (GSA) contract. These REC purchases ensured that AOC complied with the EISA 2007 requirement of 7.5% of building energy being from renewable energy. The AOC would like to continue complying with EISA 2007. The GSA energy supply contract no longer contains a REC component so AOC must take action to purchase RECs separate from GSA. 1.3 Objectives. The objective of this Renewable Energy Credit purchase is twofold: to ensure that the Architect of the Capitol continues to comply with EISA 2007 requirements that 7.5% of federal building energy be from renewable sources and to qualify for Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) credits for the Cannon office building renewal project. 1.4 Scope. The AOC is requesting firm fixed pricing for the supply of Renewable Energy Credits (RECs). The requirements are for 20,000 MWhs for each year, which includes the base year and four option years if exercised to the AOC and attributed by the percentages listed in Appendix A. The RECs required for this procurement must meet the renewable resource definition of the Center for Resource Solutions� Green-e Energy product certification, be Green-e certified, and meet the definition included in Section 1.6 in order to meet requirements of this solicitation. 1.5 Contract Type. Firm Fixed Price 1.6 Place of Performance/Hours of Operation. N/A 1.7 Period of Performance. Base Year � September 28, 2026 � September 27, 2027 Option Year 1 � September 28, 2027 � September 27, 2028 Option Year 2 � September 28, 2028 � September 27, 2029 Option Year 3 � September 28, 2029 � September 27, 2030 Option Year 4 � September 28, 2030 � September 27, 2031 1.8 Funding. Annual funding 1.9 Privacy Act. N/A 1.10 Personal Service. N/A 1.11 Security. N/A 1.12 Safety. N/A 1.13 Energy Efficiency/Compliance. EISA 2007 requirement of 7.5% of building energy being from renewable energy. 1.14 Sustainability. N/A 1.15 Key Personnel. N/A 1.16 Quality Control. N/A 1.17 Records/Data. The AOC reserves the right to validate source and transaction history as indicated above and to ensure proper reporting of sales of renewable energy credits under the resultant contract. The Contractor must meet all applicable local, state and federal documentation requirements necessary to successfully complete any contract. These records shall be made available upon request to the AOC. 1.18 Packaging/Packing/Shipping Instructions. N/A 1.19 Applicable Documents. Annual Renewable Report � Report shall meet requirements stipulated in Section 4.0 of this Statement of Work 1.20 Points of Contact. Contracting Officer � Donald Fuqua � donald.fuqua@aoc.gov COR � TBD Program Office - TBD 2.0 Definitions & Acronyms. EISA � Energy Independence and Security Act Renewable Energy � For the purposes of this contract, �renewable energy� means electric energy generated from solar, wind, ocean (including tidal, wave, current and thermal), hydro or geothermal resources RECs - Renewable Energy Credits � Unique credits that represent all of the environmental attributes or benefits of a specific quantity of renewable generation. Renewable Energy Credits are created when a renewable energy facility generates electricity. The terms renewable energy credits, tradable renewable certificates, or green tags, are equivalent terms. 3.0 Government Furnished Property (GFP). N/A 4.0 Contractor Furnished Items. title: FY26 Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) Pump Upfit
description: FY26 Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) Stormwater Pump Station - DESCRIPTION OF WORK: The Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) stormwater pump station (PS), located in the Medical District on the Charleston Peninsula, is critical infrastructure for the City of Charleston (City). The MUSC drainage basin forms a topographic low point without a natural outlet, and the PS is required to facilitate drainage. Proposed improvements include: increased pumping capacity including both pump and discharge piping capacity; improved hydraulic configuration in the wet well and inflow chamber; enclosure and conditioning of the control room; elevating all critical electrical and HVAC equipment above the design flood elevation; replacement and upgrade of electrical, instrumentation and controls, security, and lighting; construction of a new transformer pad and installation of increased capacity transformer; replacement of both wet well inflow pipes to correct pipe slope; structural supports of pipes and transformer pad; construction of a permanent bypass connection; replacement of the chain link gate; and minor grading and landscaping around the perimeter slab. The project also includes temporary pumps and piping to maintain station operations during construction. MAGNITUDE OF WORK is estimated at: $5,000,000 TO $10,000,000 North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 237110, Water and Sewer Line Related THIS ACQUISITION IS UNRESTRICTED. description: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation & Notice of Intent General Information Details Notice ID: FA9302-27-Q-0001 Notice Type: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Contracting Office: AFTC/PZZG NAICS Code: 611699 - All Other Miscellaneous Schools and Instruction PSC Code: U099 - Education/Training - Other or Other Education and Training Services Response Date: 8 September 2026, 09:00AM PST Description of Requirement This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 12.2, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The Department of War (DoW) intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with Perris Valley Aviation Services Inc, for the procurement of services for Test Parachutist Program at Edwards AFB. Notice of Intent to Sole Source Subject Description Statutory Authority 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by RFO 6.103-1 Justification There is reasonable basis to conclude that the agency can only be satisfied by Perris Valley Aviation Services, Inc. Since they are the only vendor that possesses the capability to support the drop zones, pads, and the vertical wind tunnel within 150 miles of Edwards AFB. The vendor must provide an owner-operated drop zone and aircraft. On-site maintenance facilities, FAA certified parachute riggers, and mechanics must be available. On-site vertical wind tunnel and on-site training facilities with air conditioning, padded flooring for packing of parachutes, and computers and televisions for training/debriefing purposes. Vendor must have both, door and ramp capable aircraft available for both day and night parachute operations. Skydive Perris is the only parachute operating location that currently has a wind tunnel on location. Skydive Perris is the only vendor that is currently capable of meeting the requirements of the Test Parachutist Program. Scope of Work The contractor shall provide aircraft, pilot, United States Parachute Association (USPA) course instructor(s), and facilities necessary to support the 412th OSS Test Parachutist Program (TPP) operations as defined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS) attached. Market Research A similar requirement was procured the prior year and a sources sought notice was posted in SAM.gov to find how many capable vendors would be capable of fulfilling that requirements based on the PWS. Only one response was received from BHPE LLC, stating that they were interested in this opportunity. An email was sent to them requesting their capabilities statement, but they were unresponsive. Additionally, the company is located in Oklahoma. That requirement and this current requirement calls out for the drop zones and helipad locations to be within 150 miles of Edwards AFB. If BHPE was given the opportunity to quote on this requirement, it is highly likely that they would subcontract to Perris Valley Aviation since no other small businesses are available in the local area. Other known possible sources of the service were also contacted to validate the past research. Small Business office found a potential vendor (Square One) that may be able to fulfill the service. Both Square One Parachutes and Skydive Elsinore, Inc were each contacted to which they responded that they could not provide the service required since they do not have the infrastructure in place for a vertical wind tunnel. FPDS were searched under keyword "Skydive" and limited to "Ca". All the yielded results were contract awards to Skydive Elsinore, Inc. Multiple agencies utilized their service, but they could not fulfill this requirement. Instructions to Interested Parties This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals; however, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation which shall be considered by the agency. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. title: FY26 Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) Pump Upfit
description: FY26 Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) Stormwater Pump Station - DESCRIPTION OF WORK: The Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) stormwater pump station (PS), located in the Medical District on the Charleston Peninsula, is critical infrastructure for the City of Charleston (City). The MUSC drainage basin forms a topographic low point without a natural outlet, and the PS is required to facilitate drainage. Proposed improvements include: increased pumping capacity including both pump and discharge piping capacity; improved hydraulic configuration in the wet well and inflow chamber; enclosure and conditioning of the control room; elevating all critical electrical and HVAC equipment above the design flood elevation; replacement and upgrade of electrical, instrumentation and controls, security, and lighting; construction of a new transformer pad and installation of increased capacity transformer; replacement of both wet well inflow pipes to correct pipe slope; structural supports of pipes and transformer pad; construction of a permanent bypass connection; replacement of the chain link gate; and minor grading and landscaping around the perimeter slab. The project also includes temporary pumps and piping to maintain station operations during construction. MAGNITUDE OF WORK is estimated at: $5,000,000 TO $10,000,000 North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 237110, Water and Sewer Line Related THIS ACQUISITION IS UNRESTRICTED. This solicitation is hereby posted as of 7 August 2026. Amendment 0002 - Extension of proposal due date to 11 September 2026 and is hereby posted as of 20 August 2026.

title: Mattress for Behavior Health
description: Behavioral Health Mattresses Marion VA Residential Rehabilitation Treatment Program (RRTP) 1. Background The Marion VA RRTP requires the procurement and installation of new Behavioral Health Mattresses to replace end-of-life mattresses. These mattresses are specifically designed to meet the safety, durability, and comfort standards necessary in a behavioral health setting. Procurement of mattresses meeting the specifications below will enhance patient satisfaction, reduce the risk of injury, and support the delivery of high-quality care to Veterans. 2. Scope The Contractor shall provide and install new Behavioral Health Mattresses. The mattresses supplied shall meet the minimum technical specifications outlined below. The Contractor is also responsible for removing and disposing of old mattresses and all associated waste, in accordance with facility and environmental protocols. 3. Minimum Technical Specifications All mattresses supplied must meet or exceed the following requirements: Designed and suitable for use in a behavioral health environment. Durable, RF-welded seams to eliminate the risk of accessing internal components. Full length defined perimeter to increase security and reduce fall risk. Compatible with Behavioral Health platforms and/or other VA-facility-owned frames. Maximum width: 35 inches Maximum length: 82 inches Minimum weight capacity: 500 lbs Halogen-free fire barrier, meeting all applicable fire safety regulations. Non-skid bottom cover for secure placement on bed frames. 4-way stretch top cover for enhanced comfort and durability. Foot end vents to promote airflow and mattress longevity. Core Shield layer to protect the mattress interior. Copper and gel-infused foam components to support microclimate control. Three distinct layers of foam in the head, torso, and heel sections for targeted pressure redistribution. 4. Trade-In and Waste Management The Contractor shall: Remove and dispose of all existing mattresses being replaced. Manage and dispose of all packaging and waste generated during delivery and installation. Ensure all waste disposal complies with local, state, federal, and VA environmental requirements. 5. Warranty The Contractor shall provide the manufacturer�s standard warranty for all mattresses supplied under this contract. The warranty shall cover all defects in material and workmanship. Warranty documentation must be supplied with each delivered mattress. 6. Delivery & Installation The Contractor shall coordinate all delivery and installation activities with Marion VA RRTP staff. All installation activities shall be conducted in a manner minimizing disruption to facility operations and patient care. Contractor staff must comply with all VA facility policies regarding safety, security, and infection control.

title: 36C24726Q0802 Amendment 0001
description: Questions and Answers The purpose of this amendment is provide answers to the additional questions received after the question period. The due date for offers is extended until September 08, 2026, at 12:00PM EST. **Offerors must acknowledge receipt of Amendment 0001 with their offers** Q1: Does the soundboard need to be analog or digital? A1: Digital Q2: If digital, how many faders are required? A2: 24 faders Q3: How many watts per channel on the Crown amplifiers? A3: 650W @ 8 Ohms Q4: How many channels per amplifier? A4: 2 Q5: How many HDMI outputs on the HDMI Splitter? A5: 4 Q6: The Description of Need lists an audio inserter but that is not in the requirements, please specify if an audio inserter is required. A6: Combining the audio feed from the sound board with the video feed from the camera is a requirement Q7: The Description of Need lists a digital camera, is the contractor to provide a camera? A7: Yes Q8: The Description of Need lists a HDMI switcher but that is not in the requirements, please specify if an HDMI switcher is required and if so how many inputs and outputs. A8: It is required. The switcher needs to support a minimum of 4 input channels Q9: The description of Need lists microphones but none are listed in the requirements, are microphones to be reused or is the contractor to quote microphones? A9: The existing microphones will be reused Q10: If microphones are requested to be provided, please specify how many, wired or wireless, and what type of wireless (i.e. handheld, lavalier, or head worn) A10: Not required Q11: If so, please specify if it needs to be a Pan-Tilt-Zoom (PTZ) camera or a professional/handheld camera? A11: PTZ Q12: If the customer requests a PTZ camera, do they want a control system to control the camera, HDMI switching, and audio from a wireless touch panel? A12: The camera needs to be controlled with a handheld remote Q13: If a control system is requested would the customer prefer to control volume from an iPad instead of a physical soundboard? A13: Control from a physical soundboard Q14: Is fiber distribution already in place for all rooms that the Fiber Command is to tie into? A14: No. Fiber optic cables will need to be installed to each Samsung television. Q15: If not please specify how many rooms and approximate distances required. A15: All monitors will be placed in the same room. Approximate distance is 75. Q16: Is the snake to be analog or digital? A16: Analog Q17: If analog, how long does the snake need to be? A17: Approximately 25' Q18: How is the snake to be ran? (i.e. in conduit, through basement, surface mount, through the ceiling) A18: Surface mount Q19: If digital, is there a CAT line already in place for use? A19: NA Q20: If cables need ran in the ceiling how high is the ceiling? A20: 30' Q21: Is it open rafters? A21: Yes Q22: Can we get a lift or scaffolding in to run cables or would a ladder work? A22: It is an open vaulted ceiling approximately Q23: Is the Fractal Audio AXE-FX III to be utilized for a guitar or as a digital signal processor? A23: It is to be utilized for 2 guitars and a base guitar and needs to be fully configured as part of the project. Q24: Is the contractor to provide mounts for the TVs or will those also be purchased by the customer? A24: Mounts should be provided by contractor Q25: How high are the TVs to be hung and on what type of wall? A25: One wall is cinder block and the other is sheetrock. Q26: If the contractor is to provide the TV mounts are they required to be full motion mounts? A26: Flat mounts are fine. Q27: Please provide a list of existing equipment that is to be reused. A27: The only existing equipment to be reused is the 4 existing microphones.

description: Request for Information Reference # 09012026-221118 (This is not a Request for Quotations; this is for market research purposes Sources Sought only) The Architect of the Capitol (AOC) requires the establishment of a contract to support the Capitol Power Plant�s acquisition of Renewable Energy Certificates. The resulting contract shall consist of one (1) base year and four (4) one-year option periods. This requirement shall be solicited and awarded as a firm-fixed-price contract. 1.0 General. Renewable Energy Credits 1.1 Short Description. The AOC is requesting proposals for the supply of Renewable Energy Credits (RECs) for various electrical accounts. The contract will have a base year and four (4) option years and will be priced per the total megawatt hours requested by AOC. Contractor shall supply the full REC requirement by the due date for deliveries for the base year and if exercised the option years. 1.2 Background. The Architect of the Capitol (AOC) manages approximately 18.4 million square feet of building space in over 50 buildings and 570 acres of land. The AOC has been directed by the Energy Independence and Security Act (EISA) of 2007 to continue to develop, update and implement cost effective energy comprehensive energy management and water conservation plans for all facilities administered by Congress to meet energy performance requirements for Federal buildings. In prior fiscal years, the AOC purchased RECs as a percentage of the energy procurement through the General Services Administration (GSA) contract. These REC purchases ensured that AOC complied with the EISA 2007 requirement of 7.5% of building energy being from renewable energy. The AOC would like to continue complying with EISA 2007. The GSA energy supply contract no longer contains a REC component so AOC must take action to purchase RECs separate from GSA. 1.3 Objectives. The objective of this Renewable Energy Credit purchase is twofold: to ensure that the Architect of the Capitol continues to comply with EISA 2007 requirements that 7.5% of federal building energy be from renewable sources and to qualify for Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) credits for the Cannon office building renewal project. 1.4 Scope. The AOC is requesting firm fixed pricing for the supply of Renewable Energy Credits (RECs). The requirements are for 20,000 MWhs for each year, which includes the base year and four option years if exercised to the AOC and attributed by the percentages listed in Appendix A. The RECs required for this procurement must meet the renewable resource definition of the Center for Resource Solutions� Green-e Energy product certification, be Green-e certified, and meet the definition included in Section 1.6 in order to meet requirements of this solicitation. 1.5 Contract Type. To verify compliance, the AOC requires Contractors to provide an annual report verified and certified by an independent third-party auditor. title: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION USS MCCAMPBELL (DDG-85) - MAIN REDUCTION GEAR NO. 1 LUBE OIL FLUSH
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice / Request for Information and is not a presolicitation notice, solicitation, request for proposals, request for quotations, invitation for bids, or promise to issue a solicitation. Pursuant to FAR Part 10, the Government is conducting market research to identify sources capable of satisfying the requirement, determine whether commercial products or commercial services are available or may be modified to meet the requirement, and understand customary commercial practices. Information received may support acquisition strategy, competition, and small-business set-aside decisions under FAR Parts 6 and 19. This notice does not obligate the Government to take any further action. NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center Puget Sound seeks responsible sources capable of providing all labor, supervision, facilities, materials, equipment, transportation, and qualified personnel necessary to accomplish the initial and final lube-oil flush of Main Reduction Gear (MRG) No. 1 onboard USS MCCAMPBELL (DDG-85). Work will be performed in support of U.S. Naval Ship Repair Facility and Japan Regional Maintenance Center (SRF-JRMC), Yokosuka, Japan. SCOPE OF WORK The anticipated work includes, but is not limited to: 1. Provide a qualified on-site team to accomplish the initial and final lube-oil flush of MRG No. 1. 2. Perform the work in accordance with NAVSEA Standard Items (FY26 CH-1) and the applicable Technical Work Documents, including TGI 38CGA24101A01 and TGI 38CGA24101T08. 3. Provide all required contractor-furnished material, including materials supporting cleaning and flushing work, as applicable. 4. Provide required testing and inspection records to Government quality assurance personnel. 5. Coordinate mobilization, access, travel, transportation, and shipment of contractor equipment and materials to and from Yokosuka, Japan. RADIATION PROTECTION The contractor shall comply with NAVSEA Standard Item 009-97, Radiation Protection, as applicable to and invoked for this requirement. The contractor shall ensure that its personnel, procedures, equipment, and work practices satisfy all applicable radiation-protection controls and Government access requirements before commencing work. Respondents must identify in their capability statement any qualifications, approvals, programs, or prior experience relevant to compliance with this requirement. PLACE AND ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE Place of Performance: USS MCCAMPBELL (DDG-85), U.S. Naval Ship Repair Facility and Japan Regional Maintenance Center, Yokosuka, Japan. Anticipated Period of Performance: 14 December 2026 through 28 December 2026 (15 calendar days), subject to change at the discretion of the Government. Normal work hours are anticipated to be 8:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., Monday through Friday, with a 45-minute lunch period. Additional hours outside the normal schedule may be required as directed by project management. CAPABILITY RESPONSE Interested companies that possess the capability to meet or exceed the requirement are invited to submit a concise capability statement. The response should address each item below: Company name, physical address, website, and Unique Entity ID. Point of contact, telephone number, and email address. Business size and socioeconomic status under NAICS 336611 A clear statement describing the company's technical approach and ability to perform the requirement as the prime contractor, including availability for the anticipated performance period and ability to mobilize personnel, tools, and materials to Yokosuka, Japan. Relevant past performance for work similar in type, scope, magnitude, and complexity. Include contract number, project title and description, period of performance, dollar value, customer, and a current customer point of contact with telephone number and email address. Any anticipated subcontracting, teaming, or joint-venture arrangement, including the proposed division of work. If relying on a joint venture's experience, identify projects performed together by the joint-venture members when available. Commercial-market information, customary commercial terms, industry standards, lead-time constraints, or other information that may assist the Government in developing its acquisition strategy. A statement confirming the company's ability to comply with NAVSEA Standard Item 009-97, Radiation Protection, including a brief description of relevant qualifications, approvals, programs, and experience. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Submit responses by email to denise.e.manor.civ@us.navy.mil no later than September 8th at 09:00 Pacific Time. Use the subject line: USS MCCAMPBELL (DDG-85) MRG No. 1 Lube Oil Flush - Sources Sought Response. Responses should be provided in searchable PDF or Microsoft Word format. Proprietary information must be clearly marked; however, respondents should avoid submitting classified, export-controlled, confidential personal, or otherwise sensitive information not necessary to establish capability. SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT Interested parties should be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) in accordance with FAR 52.232-33. SAM registration information is available at www.sam.gov. DISCLAIMER AND IMPORTANT NOTES This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for market-research and acquisition-planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation or commitment by the Government to award a contract. The Government will not reimburse any costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response, and no entitlement to payment or claim against the Government will arise from participation in this market research. The Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of responses or provide feedback. Failure to respond will not preclude a company from submitting an offer in response to a future solicitation, if issued. Responses to this notice will not be considered offers and will not satisfy the submission requirements of any future solicitation. The Government may use information received to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy, including whether to set aside the requirement for small business concerns. After reviewing responses, the Government may issue a solicitation on SAM.gov. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for future notices or solicitations related to this requirement.

description: Commercial Double-Deck Gas Pizza Oven � Purchase and Installation (i) Description. NIH requires one (1) commercial double-deck natural gas pizza oven, including delivery, removal and disposal of the existing oven, installation, gas connection, startup, testing, commissioning, and operator orientation in accordance with Section (vi). This is a brand-name-or-equal requirement. The Marsal (Middleby) MB-60 Stacked is identified solely as a reference for size, capacity, and capability. Equal products meeting or exceeding all salient characteristics are acceptable. CLIN 0001 � Commercial double-deck gas pizza oven, brand-name-or-equal, delivered � Qty 1 CLIN 0002 � Removal and disposal of existing oven; installation, gas connection, startup, testing, and commissioning � 1 Lot (vi) Statement of Work. Purpose. The contractor shall furnish all labor, equipment, materials, transportation, and incidental services necessary to provide NIH with one fully operational commercial-grade double-deck gas pizza oven replacing the existing deck oven. Brand-Name-or-Equal Basis. The Marsal (Middleby) MB-60 Stacked is identified as a reference for size, capacity, and capability only. Offerors proposing an equal product shall provide specifications or manufacturer cut sheets demonstrating compliance with each salient characteristic. Salient Characteristics. At a minimum, the oven shall: Be a double-stacked, two-chamber, natural gas-fired deck oven. Provide two independent baking chambers, each with usable interior dimensions of approximately 36 in. � 60 in., suitable for the existing installation location. Provide brick-lined or refractory-lined baking chambers suitable for direct-deck pizza baking. Provide a deck cooking surface capable of sustained commercial pizza baking temperatures. Provide independent thermostatic controls for each chamber over an approximate range of 300�F to 650�F. Provide total capacity of at least twelve (12) 18-inch pizzas across both chambers. Have stainless steel top and sides. Provide approximately 260,000 BTU total input. Operate on natural gas and require no more than two 120V/60Hz/1-phase electrical connections. Be ETL Sanitation listed and cETLus listed, or certified by an equivalent Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory. Accessories. The contractor shall: Receive and transport the equipment to the final installation location. Disconnect, remove, and lawfully dispose of the existing oven, including disassembly as necessary. Position, stack, level, and install the new oven and casters. Connect the existing gas service and verify proper gas pressure. Verify required clearances and compatibility with the existing ventilation system. Perform startup and verify burner operation, thermostat calibration, controls, and timers. Perform operational testing and commissioning. Coordinate all work with NIH to minimize interruption to food service operations. After-hours installation may be required. Government Responsibilities. NIH will provide site access, required utility shutoffs, existing electrical and gas infrastructure, access during scheduled installation, any desired decorative masonry fa�ade, and building modifications outside the scope of this requirement. Acceptance Criteria. Work will be accepted when: The new oven has been delivered and the existing oven removed. The new oven is fully installed and connected to the existing gas service. The contractor shall facilitate warranty service during the warranty period. Applicable Standards. Work shall comply with manufacturer installation instructions, applicable building and fire codes, OSHA requirements, applicable NFPA requirements for commercial gas cooking equipment, and NIH facility requirements. title: DAFB - Supply - Mobile Embalming Unit (MEU)
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in RFO Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The 436th Contracting Squadron (436 CONS), Dover AFB, DE, intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract for the manufacture, delivery, and on-site training of one (1) self-contained, deployable 20-foot ISO-compliant Mobile Embalming Unit (MEU) in support of the Air Force Mortuary Affairs Operations (AFMAO) global mass casualty mission. The MEU is a modified commercial, non-developmental item that must utilize a new, certified 20-foot High-Cube ISO shipping container as its structural shell. The fully integrated container and its onboard systems must be engineered for transportability via C-17, C-5, and standard flatbeds, and must operate continuously in extreme environmental conditions ranging from 0�F to 120�F. Critical Technical Specifications Include: Power & Backup: An integrated tri-fuel generator (Propane, Gasoline, Natural Gas) with an automatic electrical transfer switch compatible with 50-amp shore power (accepting both 120/240V 60Hz CONUS and 220V 50Hz OCONUS municipal power). HVAC & Bio-Containment: A specialized, high-performance single-pass HVAC system providing a continuous exchange rate of at least 15 air changes per hour (ACH) and Local Exhaust Ventilation (LEV) to maintain formaldehyde concentrations strictly below OSHA's Permissible Exposure Limit. Plumbing & Fluids Capacity: Integrated corrosion-resistant water tank storage with a combined capacity of at least 880 gallons (configured as 275 gallons fresh, 275 gallons wastewater, and 330 gallons emergency reserve). Equipment Integration: Mounting and utility connection interfaces compatible with Government-Furnished Equipment (GFE) commercial embalming machines (e.g., Portiboy, Dodge APC, Frigid, or Duotronic). Delivery & Training: FOB Destination shipping to Dover AFB, DE, with a required delivery schedule of 120 days after receipt of order (ARO). The contractor shall provide a minimum of one (1) full day (8 hours) of on-site setup, leveling, utility connection, and operational training for up to six (6) personnel upon delivery. Basis for Award: Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose technically acceptable quote represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA). Evaluation factors will be: Price: Evaluated for reasonableness. Technical Acceptability: Evaluated on a Pass/Fail basis across five (5) subfactors: Technical Approach, Designs & Specifications, Bill of Materials, Training Plan, and Quality Control/Warranty (as detailed in the attachments). Submission Instructions: All provisions, clauses, and full proposal submission instructions are contained within the attached solicitation document (Attachment 3 - Provisions and Clauses and Attachment 4 - Instructions to Offerors). Quotes must be submitted electronically to the Primary and Alternate Points of Contact listed below. Questions Due Date: 31 August 2026, at 12:30 PM EDT. Response Date/Closing Time: 4 September 2026, at 12:30 PM EDT. Primary Point of Contact: 2Lt Jonathan Goodwin Contract Manager, 436 CONS/PKB jonathan.goodwin@us.af.mil Phone: (302) 677-5033 Alternate Point of Contact: 2d Lt Travis Ambrose Contracting Officer, 436 CONS/PKB travis.ambrose.1@us.af.mil Phone: (302) 677-5033

title: Sources Sought Notice - Laboratory Cryostat System - Providence VAMC
description: 1. Purpose This is a Sources Sought Notice issued solely for market research purposes. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Regional Procurement Office East, Network Contracting Office 1, is seeking information from vendors capable of providing a laboratory cryostat system that meets the minimum technical requirements described below. This notice does not constitute a solicitation and does not commit the Government to issue a solicitation or make an award. 2. Minimum Requirement � Salient Characteristics The VA requires a cryostat system designed for producing thin, high?quality frozen sections of biological tissue used in histology, Mohs surgery, pathology, and other diagnostic applications. Vendors must be able to provide equipment that meets all of the following salient characteristics: A. Frozen Sectioning Performance Capable of producing thin, consistent, high?quality frozen tissue sections suitable for diagnostic microscopic examination. Must maintain uniform section thickness with minimal artifacts or surface defects. Must include a precision microtome mechanism that provides accurate trimming and sectioning control. B. Temperature Control & Freezing Must maintain a stable, ultra?low?temperature cryochamber for freezing biological tissues. Must provide rapid specimen?freezing capability to support time?sensitive diagnostic workflows. System must support reliable freezing that preserves cellular structures, morphology, and tissue integrity. C. Operational & Workflow Requirements Must include automated specimen retraction or equivalent safety?enhancing functionality. Must include an integrated user interface such as a touchscreen or comparable control platform that enables hands?off operation of key system functions. Must incorporate features to minimize frost accumulation and improve operator ergonomics during routine use. Must support efficient sectioning workflows suitable for environments requiring high throughput. D. Capacity Must include multiple freezing stations that allow preparation and freezing of multiple specimens. Freezing stations must support consistent and repeatable results, enabling streamlined laboratory workflows. E. Safety & Optional Features Must be designed to reduce repetitive motion strain and improve operator safety. Optional availability of built?in surface disinfection technology (such as UV or equivalent) is preferred but not required. F. Warranty Equipment must include a minimum one?year warranty covering parts and labor. 3. Domestic Manufacturing Preference The VA has a preference for domestically manufactured items, when available. Respondents must indicate: Whether the proposed end product is manufactured in the United States. If not, provide the country of origin. 4. Requested Information From Respondents Interested vendors must submit the following: Company name, address, SAM UEI, and point of contact Business size and socioeconomic classification Product specifications demonstrating capability to meet all salient characteristics listed Technical literature describing the proposed equipment Delivery lead time Information on available installation and training services Warranty terms Country where the end product is manufactured Any federal supply schedule or contract vehicles held Past performance providing similar laboratory or diagnostic equipment 5. Place of Performance Providence VA Medical Center 830 Chalkstone Avenue Providence, RI 02908 6. Submission Instructions All responses shall be submitted electronically to: Dewan.Britton@va.gov Subject line: Sources Sought � Cryostat System 36C24126Q0667 7. Disclaimer This notice is for market research purposes only. It is not a solicitation and does not obligate the Government to make an award. No contract will be awarded based solely on responses to this notice. The Government will not reimburse costs associated with responding.

title: CDC Sunflower Software License and Mobiletrak Scanner Support
description: This is a Notice of Intent, not a separate request for quote. The Government�s solicitation for this requirement is provided through the associated combined synopsis/solicitation. The Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS), on behalf of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Logistics and Property Management Services Office (LPMSO), intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract to CGI Federal, Inc. for the renewal of the Sunflower MobileTrak Site License and MobileTrak Server support. The purpose of this requirement is to provide continued access to the Sunflower MobileTrak Site License and MobileTrak Server support currently used to support CDC�s Property Management Information System (PMIS) and approximately 180 barcode scanners used for tracking, inventorying, and property management activities CDC-wide. Sunflower MobileTrak provides the software licensing and server support necessary for CDC�s barcode scanners to operate in conjunction with PMIS. The software supports inventory validation, property accountability, asset tracking, and forecasting of critical assets that may require replacement. The software works in conjunction with PMIS to link inventory validation activities to CDC�s property management system. PMIS is used to account for personal property and support property management and audit functions, and the Sunflower MobileTrak scanner environment enables CDC to maintain inventory validation within the established system. Sunflower MobileTrak supports CDC property management activities by enabling the agency to inventory and manage critical assets supporting laboratories and other agency mission functions. The annual software license and server support are necessary for continued operation of the existing barcode scanners and established PMIS property management environment. The requirement is for the renewal of the Sunflower MobileTrak Site License and MobileTrak Server support for a 12-month period of performance beginning upon award. Justification for Single Source CGI Federal, Inc. is the proposed single source for the continued use of the Sunflower MobileTrak Site License and MobileTrak Server support. This is a follow-on requirement necessary to maintain continuity of CDC�s established PMIS property management environment and ongoing inventory and property accountability activities. CGI Federal, Inc. is the sole provider of Sunflower Software Licenses and Support. CGI Federal, Inc. does not sell its software licenses or support through resellers or distributors and is the sole provider of Sunflower-configured scanners and services. The only entity able to provide support services for the proprietary Sunflower Software is CGI Federal, Inc. CDC uses approximately 180 barcode scanners supported by the Sunflower MobileTrak Site License and Server to conduct tracking, inventorying, and property management activities CDC-wide. These established scanners and the associated Sunflower environment support inventory validation, property accountability, asset management, and forecasting of critical assets. Continued use of the Sunflower MobileTrak Site License and MobileTrak Server support supports continuity of established property management operations and continued use of CDC�s existing barcode scanners and PMIS environment. Replacing the existing software environment would require transition to a new solution and could result in significant delays to the inventory process, disruption to CDC property management functions, and additional acquisition costs estimated by the program office to be approximately $45,600 more than the renewal cost. The Government requires continued access to the established Sunflower MobileTrak capabilities to maintain continuity of ongoing inventory and property management activities. Authority This acquisition is being conducted under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) FAR Part 12 � Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services and FAR Part 6.103-1 Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. For purchases not exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold, contracting officers may solicit from a single source when the Contracting Officer determines that only one source is reasonably available. Submission of Capability Statements Interested parties capable of providing the same or similar products or services must submit a capability statement electronically. Responses will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed contract, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. Capability statements must demonstrate the ability to provide Sunflower MobileTrak software and server support or an equivalent solution capable of meeting the Government�s requirements while maintaining compatibility and continuity with CDC�s existing PMIS environment, barcode scanners, and established property management operations. Capability statements must also demonstrate the ability to provide equivalent functionality for inventory validation, property accountability, asset tracking, barcode scanner integration, and forecasting of critical assets without disruption to ongoing CDC inventory and property management activities. Deadline: September 8, 2026 at 1:00 PM ET. Submit to: Vera Nordalm Contract Specialist Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS) Email: vera.nordalm@hhs.gov Copy: April Merriwether Contracting Officer Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS) Email: April.Merriwether@hhs.gov

description: USDA�s response to the New World Screwworm (NWS) is a top priority. Its National Detector Dog Training Center (NDDTC) in Newnan, GA, is expanding its NWS training program to strengthen USDA�s operational readiness and ensure canine teams are fully prepared for field conditions. Recent pilot activities in Texas demonstrated that NWS detector dogs must be safely acclimated to livestock environments including interactions with cattle, sheep, and goats to build the skills necessary for effective detection in real?world settings. To support this requirement, NDDTC must maintain goats onsite as essential training aids. Establishing appropriate housing, fencing, shelter, and utilities is a foundational step to ensure the animals� welfare, comply with applicable standards, and provide consistent access to training environments that accurately simulate operational livestock settings. The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, and expertise necessary to design, construct, and install fenced livestock enclosures, shelters, flooring, utilities, water systems, and a simulated chute?training environment to support on?site goat housing and NWS canine training. All work must comply with USDA facility, animal?welfare, and safety standards and integrate with existing NDDTC infrastructure. NOTE: Quotes are required by Sept 8. Time is of the essence for this requirement as the government requires rapid delivery. The Contractor will be required to (a) commence work under this contract immediately upon receipt of the NTP, (b) prosecute the work diligently, and (c) complete the entire work ready for use by October 30, 2026.. title: CDC CK-67 Sunflower configured ruggedized mobile computer and TC-22 Sunflower configured expandable mobile computer.
description: This is a Notice of Intent, not a separate request for quote. The Government�s solicitation for this requirement is provided through the associated combined synopsis/solicitation. The Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS), on behalf of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Logistics and Property Management Services Office (LPMSO), intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract to CGI Federal, Inc. for the purchase of Sunflower-configured Honeywell CK-67 ruggedized mobile computers, Zebra TC-22 expandable mobile computers, and associated three-year barcode scanner hardware maintenance. The purpose of this requirement is to provide CDC with ten (10) Honeywell CK-67 Sunflower-configured ruggedized mobile computers, eleven (11) Zebra TC-22 Sunflower-configured expandable mobile computers, and three-year barcode scanner hardware maintenance for all twenty-one (21) scanners. The equipment is required to support CDC property management operations and must operate with the agency�s existing Sunflower MobileTrak site license, MobileTrak server license, and Property Management Information System (PMIS). The CK-67 and TC-22 scanners provide the hardware capability necessary to support CDC-wide property tracking, inventorying, management, and asset forecasting. The Sunflower-based property management environment enables CDC to inventory and manage critical assets supporting its laboratories and other mission-support functions and assists the agency in identifying critical assets that may require replacement. The required scanners must be Sunflower-configured to maintain compatibility with CDC�s existing MobileTrak and PMIS environment. The requirement aligns with the Department of Health and Human Services Sunflower-based property management system currently used to manage critical Government assets. The requirement includes three-year barcode scanner hardware maintenance for all twenty-one (21) Sunflower-configured scanners. Justification for Single Source CGI Federal, Inc. is the proposed single source for this requirement and is the only responsible source capable of providing the required Sunflower-configured scanners and associated services. CGI Federal, Inc. is the sole provider of Sunflower software licenses and support. CGI Federal, Inc. does not sell its Sunflower software licenses or support through resellers or distributors and is the sole provider of Sunflower-configured scanners and related services. CDC�s existing property management environment relies on Sunflower MobileTrak and PMIS to support agency-wide property tracking, inventory management, and asset forecasting. The required CK-67 and TC-22 scanners must be configured specifically for compatibility with this existing environment. Continued use of Sunflower-configured scanning equipment is necessary to maintain continuity of CDC�s established property management operations. Equipment that is not configured for the existing Sunflower environment would not satisfy the Government�s requirement for compatibility with its current MobileTrak and PMIS infrastructure. Failure to obtain the required Sunflower-compatible scanners could result in significant delays in CDC inventory activities, inaccurate forecasting of critical assets, disruption to mission-support functions, and an adverse impact on the agency�s ability to perform its property management responsibilities. Because CGI Federal, Inc. is the sole provider of Sunflower-configured scanners and related services, no other source can provide the required supplies and services while maintaining the compatibility necessary for CDC�s existing Sunflower property management environment. Authority This acquisition is being conducted under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12 � Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services and FAR 6.103-1 Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Submission of Capability Statements Interested parties capable of providing the same or similar products or services must submit a capability statement electronically. Responses will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed contract, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. Capability statements must demonstrate the ability to provide Honeywell CK-67 ruggedized mobile computers and Zebra TC-22 expandable mobile computers configured for use with CDC�s existing Sunflower MobileTrak and PMIS environment, together with the required three-year hardware maintenance. Capability statements must also demonstrate the ability to provide equipment and services that maintain compatibility and continuity with CDC�s existing Sunflower-based property management environment without disruption to CDC-wide property tracking, inventory management, and asset forecasting activities. Deadline: September 8, 2026 at 1:00 PM ET Submit to: Vera Nordalm Contract Specialist Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS) Email: vera.nordalm@hhs.gov Copy: April Merriwether Contracting Officer Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS) Email: April.Merriwether@hhs.gov

description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes as the only solicitation. Quotes are being requested and a written solicitation is attached. Solicitation number W913E526QA004 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ) for Antarctic Airfield Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) Fire Suppression System. This requirement is a total set-aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov/faroverhaul. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Cold Regions Research and Engineering Laboratory (CRREL), Engineering Research Branch (ERB) has a requirement for delivery and installation of six (6) Compressed Air Foam System (CAFS) firefighting systems for integration as complete Antarctic Airfield Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) vehicles. The Contractor shall also provide training on operation of the suppression systems and will be required to ship the completed systems to a to be determined CONUS integration contractor facility. Product Specifications: A partly custom solution is required consisting of commercially available wheeled and tracked, low ground pressure, 7.5-ton payload vehicles that will have separate, integrated commercially available fire suppression systems. This requirement is for the fire suppression portion of the total ARFF solution. Some minor modification of these commercial products may be necessary to meet the needs of Antarctic functionality, specifically to ensure mechanical systems operate down to -30F. Please reference the attached RFQ W913E526QA008 for instructions and applicable provisions and clauses. The Government intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer represents the Best Value, considering price and non-price factors. The basis for award will be an acceptable quote, the price of which may not be the lowest.The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers: 1) Technical capability to comply with specification, delivery requirements, and warranty provisions as outlined in Section C, Description of Requirement (DOR). 2) Past experience and competency in the nature of the requested mission. 3) Total price to fulfill the Government�s requirement in its entirety. Price will be evaluated for reasonableness and completeness. A technically acceptable quote is one that clearly represents the ability to satisfy the minimum specified requirements outlined in Section C, DOR and the quote submission instructions outlined in Section L, Instructions to Offerors. The quote shall provide sufficient information for the Government to determine its level of confidence in the ability of the Offeror to meet the requirements. title: CDC CK-67 Sunflower configured ruggedized mobile computer and TC-22 Sunflower configured expandable mobile computer.
description: This is a Notice of Intent, not a separate request for quote. The Government�s solicitation for this requirement is provided through the associated combined synopsis/solicitation. The Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS), on behalf of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Logistics and Property Management Services Office (LPMSO), intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract to CGI Federal, Inc. for the purchase of Sunflower-configured Honeywell CK-67 ruggedized mobile computers, Zebra TC-22 expandable mobile computers, and associated three-year barcode scanner hardware maintenance. The purpose of this requirement is to provide CDC with ten (10) Honeywell CK-67 Sunflower-configured ruggedized mobile computers, eleven (11) Zebra TC-22 Sunflower-configured expandable mobile computers, and three-year barcode scanner hardware maintenance for all twenty-one (21) scanners. The equipment is required to support CDC property management operations and must operate with the agency�s existing Sunflower MobileTrak site license, MobileTrak server license, and Property Management Information System (PMIS). The CK-67 and TC-22 scanners provide the hardware capability necessary to support CDC-wide property tracking, inventorying, management, and asset forecasting. The Sunflower-based property management environment enables CDC to inventory and manage critical assets supporting its laboratories and other mission-support functions and assists the agency in identifying critical assets that may require replacement. The required scanners must be Sunflower-configured to maintain compatibility with CDC�s existing MobileTrak and PMIS environment. The requirement aligns with the Department of Health and Human Services Sunflower-based property management system currently used to manage critical Government assets. The requirement includes three-year barcode scanner hardware maintenance for all twenty-one (21) Sunflower-configured scanners. Justification for Single Source CGI Federal, Inc. is the proposed single source for this requirement and is the only responsible source capable of providing the required Sunflower-configured scanners and associated services. CGI Federal, Inc. is the sole provider of Sunflower software licenses and support. CGI Federal, Inc. does not sell its Sunflower software licenses or support through resellers or distributors and is the sole provider of Sunflower-configured scanners and related services. CDC�s existing property management environment relies on Sunflower MobileTrak and PMIS to support agency-wide property tracking, inventory management, and asset forecasting. The required CK-67 and TC-22 scanners must be configured specifically for compatibility with this existing environment. Continued use of Sunflower-configured scanning equipment is necessary to maintain continuity of CDC�s established property management operations. Equipment that is not configured for the existing Sunflower environment would not satisfy the Government�s requirement for compatibility with its current MobileTrak and PMIS infrastructure. Failure to obtain the required Sunflower-compatible scanners could result in significant delays in CDC inventory activities, inaccurate forecasting of critical assets, disruption to mission-support functions, and an adverse impact on the agency�s ability to perform its property management responsibilities. Because CGI Federal, Inc. is the sole provider of Sunflower-configured scanners and related services, no other source can provide the required supplies and services while maintaining the compatibility necessary for CDC�s existing Sunflower property management environment. Authority This acquisition is being conducted under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12 � Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services and FAR 6.103-1 Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Submission of Capability Statements Interested parties capable of providing the same or similar products or services must submit a capability statement electronically. Responses will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed contract, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. Capability statements must demonstrate the ability to provide Honeywell CK-67 ruggedized mobile computers and Zebra TC-22 expandable mobile computers configured for use with CDC�s existing Sunflower MobileTrak and PMIS environment, together with the required three-year hardware maintenance. Capability statements must also demonstrate the ability to provide equipment and services that maintain compatibility and continuity with CDC�s existing Sunflower-based property management environment without disruption to CDC-wide property tracking, inventory management, and asset forecasting activities. Deadline: September 8, 2026 at 1:00 PM ET Submit to: Vera Nordalm Contract Specialist Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS) Email: vera.nordalm@hhs.gov Copy: April Merriwether Contracting Officer Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS) Email: April.Merriwether@hhs.gov

title: Installation of Livestock Holding Pens and Chutes
description: USDA�s response to the New World Screwworm (NWS) is a top priority. Its National Detector Dog Training Center (NDDTC) in Newnan, GA, is expanding its NWS training program to strengthen USDA�s operational readiness and ensure canine teams are fully prepared for field conditions. Recent pilot activities in Texas demonstrated that NWS detector dogs must be safely acclimated to livestock environments including interactions with cattle, sheep, and goats to build the skills necessary for effective detection in real?world settings. To support this requirement, NDDTC must maintain goats onsite as essential training aids. Establishing appropriate housing, fencing, shelter, and utilities is a foundational step to ensure the animals� welfare, comply with applicable standards, and provide consistent access to training environments that accurately simulate operational livestock settings. The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, and expertise necessary to design, construct, and install fenced livestock enclosures, shelters, flooring, utilities, water systems, and a simulated chute?training environment to support on?site goat housing and NWS canine training. All work must comply with USDA facility, animal?welfare, and safety standards and integrate with existing NDDTC infrastructure. NOTE: Quotes are required by Sept 8. Time is of the essence for this requirement as the government requires rapid delivery. The Contractor will be required to (a) commence work under this contract immediately upon receipt of the NTP, (b) prosecute the work diligently, and (c) complete the entire work ready for use by October 16, 2026..
